name: Vladimir Lenin
role: Bolshevik revolutionary and head of Soviet government (1917–1924)
summary: Lenin was the Bolshevik leader who led the October 1917 insurrection and headed the Soviet government until 1924, arguing for a vanguard party, the dictatorship of the proletariat and soviets in place of parliament. In power his government nationalised land, banks, foreign trade and large industry, separated church and state, liberalised marriage and divorce, dissolved the Constituent Assembly, outlawed opposition parties and used terror, before turning in 1921 to the New Economic Policy of controlled markets and concessions.
